newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil resist Chicago pressure.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil resist Chicago pressure.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices resisted downward pressure from the Chicago soy futures market on Tuesday afternoon.
Chicago soybeans hit new contract lows in spill-over sentiment from Monday's USDA report which pegged U.S. soybean acreage at 70.85 million, the highest for 15 years.
However, traders Europe were more concerned about the stock situation in South America and the effect of a strong dollar on the market.
Traders said South American soybeans have never been sold so far forward at this time of year before and there was some slight concern over the stock situation.

They said the strong dollar was also a factor with crushers finding their margins squeezed. "Crushers are having a job finding a margin with the dollar so strong, and they are calling the tune, not Chicago," said another trader.
Palm oil sellers reduced their asking prices by a further $2.50 a tonne during the afternoon in anticipation of lower prices in Malaysia on Wednesday.
Earlier prices had not fall as much as expected following a rebound towards the close of the Malaysian market on refiner buying.
"One major player has been buying, but we don't know if they are covering positions or just trying to support the market," said one trader.
Figures issued by Malaysian cargo surveyor Caleb Brett putting local palm oil exports during June at 634,753 tonnes against 641,950 in May had no impact on the market.
At the close Dutch soy oil was unchanged to 0.50 guilders down after Jul traded at 104.50 in a switch with Aug at 104 guilders.
In outright trading Nov/Jan fetched 99.75 and 99.25 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Rape oil finished with sellers 0.50 guilders up after Jul traded at 104.50 and Aug/Sep at 101.75 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
In the palm oil sector one additional trade was reported during the afternoon when June crude palm oil (CPO) fetched $527.50 a tonne cif.
CPO sellers closed $2.50 down while products were $5 down to $2.50 up.
Coconut oil closed $2.50 down while palmkernel oil was $2.50 up to $2.50 down in a neglected lauric oil market.
